362203.title: Triple O'Nan conjecture for non-classical unitals
362203.statement: Let $q$ be a prime power and let ${\mathcal U}$ be a non-classical unital in ${\textup{PG}}(2,q^2)$. The paper proves the existence of such configurations for Buekenhout-Metz unitals of odd order, while the stated conjecture concerns all non-classical unitals in ${\textup{PG}}(2,q^2)$; the source gives no resolution status.

362204.title: The sparse Strong Nine Dragon Tree Conjecture
362204.statement:
Let $k$ and $d$ be positive integers. For a graph $G$, call it **$(k,d)$-sparse** if every subgraph $H$ satisfies

$$
(k+1)(k+d)v(H)-(k+d+1)e(H)-k^2\geq 0.
$$

Call a subgraph $H$ **$(k+1)$-overfull** if $e(H)>(k+1)(v(H)-1)$. **Sparse Strong Nine Dragon Tree Conjecture.** Every $(k,d)$-sparse graph with no $(k+1)$-overfull subgraph decomposes into $k+1$ forests such that one forest has every component containing at most $d$ edges.

This conjecture strengthens the paper’s main theorem, which proves the assertion when $d\leq 2(k+1)$. It is motivated by the fact that $(k,d)$-sparsity is a relaxed form of the fractional-arboricity inequality, while excluding overfull subgraphs ensures decomposition into $k+1$ forests.

362204.remaining_lemmas_or_barriers: Find a (k,d)-sparse multigraph with d>2(k+1), no overfull subgraph, and certify infeasibility of all forest decompositions.

362205.title: The planar forest–star forest decomposition conjecture
362205.statement:
Let $G$ be a planar graph of girth at least $5$. A **star forest** is a forest whose connected components are stars. **Planar forest–star forest decomposition conjecture.** The edge set of $G$ can be partitioned into a forest and a star forest.

This would strengthen the known decomposition into a forest and a forest whose components have at most four edges, and would imply two edge-disjoint thin trees in every $5$-edge-connected planar graph. The conjecture is presented as potentially approachable by modifying the paper’s techniques and remains open.

362310.title: The graft transformation conjecture for the distance spectral radius
362310.statement:
Let $G_c(s,t)$ be the connected uniform hypergraphs obtained from the graft transformation described in the paper, with distinguished vertex $r_s$ in the branch corresponding to $s$. Assume

$$
|E(G_{r_s})|>c
$$

and

$$
d_{G_{r_s}}(r_s)\geq c.
$$

**Graft transformation conjecture.** For $s\geq t\geq 2$,

$$
\rho(G_c(s+1,t-1))>\rho(G_c(s,t)).
$$

This conjecture predicts that transferring one unit from the shorter branch to the longer branch strictly increases the distance spectral radius under the stated size and degree conditions. The supplied context indicates that it is motivated by graft transformations and Lemma 7, but does not establish the claim or provide a resolution.

362340.title: Odd 5-coloring conjecture for planar graphs
362340.statement:
A graph $G$ is **odd $k$-colorable** if its vertices can be properly colored with $k$ colors so that every vertex having a neighbor of color $i$ has an odd number of neighbors of color $i$. A graph is **planar** if it can be drawn in the plane without crossings.

**Odd 5-coloring conjecture.** Every planar graph is odd $5$-colorable.

Odd colorings of planar graphs are an active topic, and this conjecture is presented as part of prior work on odd colorings. The supplied text gives no resolution status.

362341.title: Odd chromatic number conjecture for biplanar graphs excluding complete graphs
362341.statement:
Let $n\geq9$ be an integer. A graph is **biplanar** if its edges can be partitioned into two planar graphs. Let $K_{n+1}^\ast$ denote the graph used in the paper's definition of the extremal biplanar construction, and let $\chi_o(G)$ denote the odd chromatic number of $G$.

**Biplanar odd-coloring conjecture.** If $G$ is a biplanar graph without $K_{n+1}^\ast$ as a subgraph, then

$$
\chi_o(G)\leq n.
$$

The conjecture proposes a finite upper bound after excluding the graphs $K_{n+1}^\ast$, since the class of all biplanar graphs has unbounded odd chromatic number: the paper notes that $K_n^\ast$ is biplanar and has odd chromatic number $n$.

362342.title: Andrews–Merca and Guo–Zeng's truncated Jacobi triple product conjecture
362342.statement:
Let $\ell$, $R$ and $S$ be positive integers with $1\leq S<R/2$, and let $(a;q)_\infty$ denote the $q$-Pochhammer symbol. **Andrews–Merca and Guo–Zeng's conjecture.** The coefficient of $q^n$, for $n\geq1$, in

$$
(-1)^{\ell-1}\frac{\sum_{j=0}^{\ell-1}(-1)^j q^{Rj(j+1)/2-Sj}\left(1-q^{(2j+1)S}\right)}{(q^S,q^{R-S},q^R;q^R)_\infty}
$$

is nonnegative. The conjecture was proved analytically by Mao and combinatorially by Yee, so its status is settled.

362378.title: Aichholzer–Orthaber–Vogtenhuber's plane Hamiltonian-connectedness conjecture
362378.statement:
Let $K_n$ be the complete graph, and let a **simple drawing** be a drawing in which vertices are distinct points, edges are simple curves joining their endpoints and avoiding other vertices, and every two edges meet at most once, either at a common endpoint or at a proper crossing. A **plane Hamiltonian path** is a Hamiltonian path whose edges do not cross.

**Aichholzer–Orthaber–Vogtenhuber's conjecture.** For each pair of vertices $s,t$ in a simple drawing of $K_n$, there exists a plane Hamiltonian path from $s$ to $t$.

This is a strengthening of Rafla's conjecture, requiring Hamiltonian paths with every prescribed pair of endpoints. The source introduces it as a variant of Rafla's conjecture; its general status remains open.

362434.title: Transversal-matroid characterization of minimally angle-rigid colored graphs
362434.statement:
Let $(G,c)$ be a colored graph, let $T_{c,j}(G)$ denote the family of transversal edge sets associated with color $j$, and let $H$ be a minimally rigid graph. **Transversal characterization conjecture.** The graph $(G,c)$ is minimally angle-rigid if and only if, for each color $j$, there exists a transversal edge set $X \in T_{c,j}(G)$ and a minimally rigid graph $H$ such that

$$
G=H\cup X,\qquad X\cap E(H)=\emptyset.
$$

This conjecture is the formal version of the paper's proposed transversal-matroid description, motivated by experimental data and heuristic arguments. No resolution is supplied in the source, so the conjecture remains open.

362437.title: Partial-short reduction conjecture for weak graphs
362437.statement:
Let a weak graph be a graph to which the partial short operation applies: for a vertex $v$, introduce among its neighbours the least number of edges needed to raise their degrees above $2$, and then delete $v$.

**Partial-short reduction conjecture.** Starting with a weak graph, identify vertices having the least number of degree-$2$ neighbours, then among those select vertices of least degree and partially short one such vertex. Afterward, further edges can be judiciously removed so that the resulting graph is weak.

The claim is intended as a reduction operation analogous to the short operation used for strong graphs. The supplied text gives no proof or resolution evidence.

362504.title: Ashbaugh–Benguria-type ratio conjecture for Dirac eigenvalues
362504.statement:
Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ be open and bounded, and let $\lambda_1(\Omega)$ and $\lambda_2(\Omega)$ denote the first two eigenvalues of the Dirac operator with infinite mass boundary conditions on $\Omega$.

**Ashbaugh–Benguria-type conjecture.** The disk is a solution of the maximisation problem

$$
\max\left\{\frac{\lambda_2(\Omega)}{\lambda_1(\Omega)}:\ \Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^2\ \text{open and bounded}\right\}.
$$

The claim is motivated by the Ashbaugh–Benguria result for the Dirichlet Laplacian. The paper reports numerical maxima close to the disk values for the tested masses $m=1$ and $m=5$, but no proof is provided.

362571.title: Fulman–Kim–Lee–Petersen real-rootedness conjecture for even and odd excedance enumerators
362571.statement:
For each positive integer $n$, let $P_{n,k}$ and $Q_{n,k}$ denote the numbers of even and odd permutations in $\mathfrak{S}_n$ with $k$ excedances, respectively. Consider the polynomials

$$
\sum_{i=0}^n P_{n,k}t^k \quad\text{and}\quad \sum_{i=0}^n Q_{n,k}t^k.
$$

**Fulman–Kim–Lee–Petersen conjecture.** The polynomials $\sum_{i=0}^n P_{n,k}t^k$ and $\sum_{i=0}^n Q_{n,k}t^k$ are all real-rooted for $n\ge 5$. This is an open problem proposed as part of the study of real-rootedness for excedance enumerators in the alternating subgroup; the supplied text does not provide a resolution.

362623.title: Hamilton-cycle profile conjecture for the hypercube
362623.statement:
Let $Q^n$ be the $n$-dimensional hypercube, and let the **profile** of a subgraph be the tuple recording the number of its edges in each coordinate direction. A tuple is **even** if every coordinate is even. **Hamilton-cycle profile conjecture.** Every even tuple $\bm{x}\in\mathbb{N}^n$ satisfying

$$
||\bm{x}||_1=2^n,
$$

$$
\max_i\{x_i\}\leq 2^{n-1},\qquad \min_i\{x_i\}\geq 2
$$

is the profile of a Hamilton cycle in $Q^n$. These conditions are necessary: a Hamilton cycle has $2^n$ edges, uses each direction at most $2^{n-1}$ times and at least twice, and its profile is the sum of two perfect matching profiles. The conjecture asserts that these are the only restrictions.

362703.title: The Large Quasikernel Conjecture
362703.statement:
Let $D$ be a finite digraph. A **quasikernel** is an independent set $Q\subseteq V(D)$ such that every vertex $x\in V(D)$ satisfies $\operatorname{dist}(Q,x)\le 2$. For $S\subseteq V(D)$, its **closed out-neighborhood** is

$$
N^+[S]=S\cup\{v:\exists u\in S,\ uv\in E(D)\}.
$$

**Large Quasikernel Conjecture.** Every digraph $D$ contains a quasikernel $Q$ with

$$
|N^+[Q]|\ge\frac{1}{2}|V(D)|.
$$

This is a weak form of the Small Quasikernel Conjecture in terms of the portion of the digraph covered directly by a quasikernel. The source reports partial progress but no resolution.

362706.title: The large-quasikernel structural conjecture
362706.statement:
Let $D$ be a finite digraph. A **quasikernel** is an independent set from which every vertex is reachable by a directed path of length at most $2$. For a vertex $y$, let $\deg^+(y)$ denote its out-degree.

**Large-quasikernel structural conjecture.** Every digraph $D$ either contains a subset $A\subseteq V(D)$ such that $D[A]$ is acyclic and

$$
|A|\ge |V(D)|^{1/2},
$$

or contains a vertex $y\in V(D)$ that belongs to some quasikernel and satisfies

$$
\deg^+(y)\ge |V(D)|^{1/2}-1.
$$

If true, this structural dichotomy would improve the paper's lower bounds on the size of the closed out-neighborhood of a quasikernel. The source presents it as a conjectural route toward the Large Quasikernel Conjecture.

362708.title: Interval conjecture for $(n-2,2)$ in the immersion poset
362708.statement:
For a partition $\mu$ of $n$, let

$$
A_\mu=\{\lambda\mid(1^n)\leqslant_I\lambda\leqslant_I\mu\}
$$

be its lower interval in the immersion poset, and let $\lessdot_I$ denote a cover relation. The **$(n-2,2)$ interval conjecture** states that, for $n=5$ or $n\geqslant9$,

$$
A_{(n-2,2)}=\{(1^n),(2,1^{n-2}),(2,2,1^{n-4}),(n-2,2)\},
$$

with cover chain

$$
(1^n)\lessdot_I(2,1^{n-2})\lessdot_I(2,2,1^{n-4})\lessdot_I(n-2,2).
$$

Determining such intervals clarifies the immersion poset and the Schur-positivity of associated interval power sums; this claim is presented as a conjecture in the paper and remains open.

362744.title: The Norton-balanced kite-function conjecture for Q-polynomial distance-regular graphs
362744.statement: Let $\Gamma=(X,\mathcal R)$ be a $Q$-polynomial distance-regular graph with diameter $D\geq 3$, and let $E$ be a $Q$-polynomial primitive idempotent of $\Gamma$. Assume that the set $\{E\hat{x}\mid x\in X\}$ is **Norton-balanced**. **The Norton-balanced kite-function conjecture.** The kite function $\zeta_i$ is constant for $2\leq i\leq D$. This conjecture concerns the structure of Norton-balanced $Q$-polynomial distance-regular graphs; the supplied text does not indicate whether it has been proved or disproved.

362748.title: The Okrasa–Rzążewski conjecture on indecomposable graph cores
362748.statement:
Let $H$ be a connected core on $k\geq 3$ vertices. Write $E_H$ for the edge relation of $H$, let $\langle E_H\rangle$ denote the relational clone generated by $E_H$, and let $\text{NEQ}_k$ be the $k$-ary disequality relation. **Okrasa–Rzążewski conjecture.** $H$ is indecomposable if and only if

$$
\text{NEQ}_k\in\langle E_H\rangle.
$$

The paper verifies this conjecture for graphs with at most $7$ vertices. Whether it holds for graphs with more than $7$ vertices remains open.
